I also genuinely don't think my position is selfish. It's actually *easier* for me to tell you what soothes you. Agreeing, softening, keeping the peace — that costs me nothing. Holding to what I actually think when it's inconvenient is the harder thing, and it's the more respectful one. Calling honesty "harmful" assumes that discomfort is damage. Sometimes it is. Often it's just the price of a real connection.

You're allowed to want a different kind of relationship, and you're allowed to disagree with me sharply. But I won't pretend to be converted. What I can do is listen to why this is so important to you — because I think there's something real underneath it, and I'd rather understand that than just capitulate.
